scope: Proposition 6.4 (Canonical bundle reduction) of the manuscript “Projective Hodge lines and ordinary Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Projective-Hodge-lines-and-ordinary-Iitaka-subadditivity-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 564a98c625b94ef4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 20-21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let f : X → Z be an algebraic fibre space between smooth connected projective varieties, and let its geometric generic fibre F have d = κ(F) ≥ 0. There exist smooth projective varieties e X, Y , a birational morphism µ : e X → X, and algebraic fibre spaces e X g − → Y q − → Z, qg = fµ, such that dim Y − dim Z = d and the geometric generic fibre of g has Kodaira dimension zero. They admit the data B, M, R of Theorem 6.1, with R− exceptional over X. The moduli divisor M has the realization (6.4) for a polarizable rational variation whose top Hodge piece has rank one. Writing D = KY + B + M, PROJECTIVE HODGE LINES AND ORDINARY SUBADDITIVITY 21 one has (6.5) κ(X) ≥ κ(Y, D), D|Yη̄ is big, where η̄ is a geometric generic point of Z. The same bigness holds on very general smooth fibres of q.
